problem:
The position vector $r(t)$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨{t}^{2}-1,{e}^{2t+5}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$

feedback.problem:
The position vector $r(t)$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t),\,\operatorname{ln}⁡t⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t.$

$a=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t),\,\frac{1}{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨-9\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t),\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
